OOTECH OOCHU TAKEHNIYA TINKLES ST. MARK, eBible.org, https://ebible.org/bea/

The edition's own statement of rights (from eBible.org's page for this translation):
> "Public Domain
Language: Dane Zaa (Beaver)
Translation by: Rev. A. C. Garrioch
Originally published in 1886 by the British and Foriegn Bible Society. This book is now in the PUBLIC DOMAIN."
(from eBible.org's page for this translation, https://ebible.org/bea/copyright.htm)

Why this is public domain:
Translator: Rev. Alfred Campbell Garrioch, 1848-1934 (died 1934, Canada; the Church Missionary Society Anglican missionary who was born in Manitoba and retired to Portage la Prairie). First publication: 1886 (eBible says British and Foreign Bible Society; the Canadiana catalogue record at https://www.canadiana.ca/view/oocihm.14252 lists an SPCK London edition in 1886). US: published in 1886, before 1931, so public domain in the United States. Origin country: Canada (translator's country) and the United Kingdom (place of publication). Canada's life plus 50 years ended in 1985 for a 1934 death; the United Kingdom's life plus 70 years ended in 2005. The translator died in 1934, so the text is public domain in every country with a term of life + 90 years or less, whatever the exact rule of Canada or the United Kingdom. Nobody besides Garrioch is named for this text.

Sources of these facts:
eBible.org copyright page (https://ebible.org/bea/copyright.htm); Garrioch's life dates and publication history from bible.com (https://www.bible.com/versions/2327-be86sy-makr and https://www.bible.com/versions/1664) and the Canadiana record (https://www.canadiana.ca/view/oocihm.14252).

The verse-per-line archive holds the Bible text in one file, one verse per line, each line starting with its reference (book, chapter:verse); its SQL and XML copies of the same text, eBible.org's description page, style sheet and signature are left out of the source.

note: The verse-numbered twin of ebible-bea-bd334ab0, for the parallel verses measure only (#35): its tag is verse-numbers alone, which no mixture selects, so it never enters training. eBible.org rebuilds this zip often; the checksum covers the files inside.
